newsitem.title: UK: LDC debt limps into Christmas, only Bulgaria stirs.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt limps into Christmas, only Bulgaria stirs.

text.p: Emerging debt trade limped towards the Christmas break with most players away on holiday and little activity to lift traders out of their langour.
"This morning is for having coffee and mince pies and leaving early," said one trader here. "They'll probably have the same fizzle when they open in New York."
Bulgarian debt continued to languish as the country remained without a prime minister after the surprise resignation of Zhan Videnov as premier and party leader at the weekend.

Though a congress of the ruling Socialist party elected Georgi Parvanov as its new leader early on Tuesday, Parvanov told Reuters in Sofia the party had yet to debate whether Videnov would return as premier.
The party has come under fire for past economic failings and needs strong leadership to push through painful economic reform. The new premier will be announced on December 28.
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH24A=RR, which represent pure Bulgarian risk, were 1/8 weaker at 51-1/8.

Meanwhile the hostage crisis in Peru showed little sign of resolution before Christmas despite the release of 225 captives on Sunday night. Peruvian Citi debt PEFLG91=RR held steady at its lower 116-00 level.
Elsewhere Russian and Latin American prices were mainly unchanged.

The Brady market will be closed in London on Wednesday and Thursday for the Christmas break but reopens on Friday. The New York market will be closed on Wednesday but trading resumes there on Thursday, traders said. -- Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
